application: scripts/depthn_screen_amended_verdict.py --run-binding <the screen-r2 adoption record> <its sha256> --run-amendment <this file> <its sha256>: the screen-r2 binding requires this record (pinned in RUN_AMENDMENTS), and the final-fairness gate then runs as scripts/depthn_fairness_final.py final_gate(..., bands='exact'). The drift diagnosis is scripts/depthn_fairness_final.py window --alive-bands exact. The four adopted rule files, their logic and their sha256s are unchanged.
computed_before: No outcome statistic of screen-r2 has been computed or inspected: no score, win, paired difference, interval or bound, of either arm. This amendment is derived from fairness data only (Foul Play iteration rates, their budget strata, turns and alive counts): flag-1 (at 100 cumulative pairs, ratio, weighted 0.937, acknowledged benign), flag-2 (at 150 cumulative pairs, drift, window from completion 216, weighted 1.112), the flag-1 diagnosis (finer 1.045, within), the flag-2 window diagnosis (finer 1.088, not within) and the whole-run diagnosis at 150 cumulative pairs (finer 1.0515, not within; final_gate on the same data: difference 0.05155), cited by sha256 in evidence. In the finer re-stratification the matched strata read 0.98-1.01; every large deviation sits in the coarse 1-2 alive endgame buckets, which pool one and two alive Pokemon. The panel was stopped at flag-2; the result files were counted by name only (panel_state), never read for this record. No exact-alive-band reading ({1}, {2}, {3-4}, {5-6}) of any screen-r2 data had been computed when this record was made or revised.
decided_by: the lead (search, V2, CUDA): one outcome-blind amendment of the fairness alive bands. Flag 2 is acknowledged benign and the screen resumes only under rule.acknowledgement; otherwise the run stops and goes back to the lead, with no second amendment
